name: runMessage
summary: One instruction card at a time is enforced by runMessage(): a chain of returns whose single result drawRunHUD renders once per frame.
detail: Priority order: FIRST FLIGHT intro, black hole, star dive, Starfall running, Starfall result, MEET lesson (tag TRY THIS), tier banner, Starfall armed, say line, hint ladder (tag FLIGHT TIP). There is no second in-arena instruction surface; drawPowerStatus prints countdowns and the header prints score and level only. The death screen is a separate state and draws its coach line there.

name: firstMeet
summary: Ten guards decide whether a first-encounter lesson fires; every one of them defers rather than spends, because G.seen is set only after all pass.
detail: In order: G.intro, already-seen or no MEET row, LAB.on, 9s spacing (G.meetNext), a running hop rehearsal, a banner younger than 2.4s, a landFx/secFx payoff card, bhActive(), soft-lesson-waits-for-G.seen.single, and for hard lessons only: no live timed reward and no armed lethal shard within 1.2 rad on the player's ring. Sets G.teach=2.8, G.teachKind='see', fires cueLesson().

name: soft lesson gate on G.seen.single
summary: No reward lesson may fire until the red-shard lesson has landed on the device: firstMeet returns early while soft && !G.seen.single.
detail: Measured on a fresh device before this guard: combo at 5.4s, music 14.4s, orbit 24.7s, lapcost 33.9s, and single - the only lesson about the thing that kills - at 44.3s. The SHIELDS FULL say line carries the same gate at runtime.js:8601.

name: death re-arms the killer's lesson
summary: Dying to a mechanic whose lesson was already spent deletes its seen bit and sets seen2, so the next encounter re-offers the sentence once, in soft form.
detail: Capped at once per type per device by cometloop:seen2. The re-offer is soft because firstMeet reads soft = MEET[type].soft || G.seen2[type], so a veteran is never slow-motioned twice. Never from a lab death. smoke.mjs drives a gate death and asserts both the clear and the cap.

name: lab lesson guards
summary: Two separate writers could spend a lesson in POWERUP TESTING - firstMeet's sentence and the pickup shortcut - and both are guarded on LAB.on.
detail: firstMeet returns early when LAB.on (runtime.js:5570); the pickup path that treats taking a musical orb as its introduction is guarded independently at runtime.js:8559. die()'s re-arm is guarded too. The harness found the second guard: one looked like the whole job and there were two. smoke.mjs snapshots localStorage across a whole lab session and fails if a key changes.

name: pickType insist loop
summary: While an unlocked formation's lesson has not landed, that shape is the next spawn - lowest tier first - so the curriculum cannot be lost to pool odds.
detail: Walks TIERS from 0 to the current tier and returns the first type with no seen bit, subject to the same board rules the pool uses (twin/blinktwin need 2 rings, one wall at a time, no gate beside a saucer). The newest tier gets a 4s banner head start first. Density is untouched - same spawn, different shape. The orb half of the rule: an unseen orb re-fires its lesson every frame it is on the board and an unseen orb that expires clears its placed flag and is re-placed.

name: say / annPump
summary: Announcement lines queue with a priority and a TTL and can be dropped unread: annPump refuses to promote one while a banner is younger than 2.6s.
detail: say(str,pri,ttl) refuses duplicates already queued; default TTL 14s but most orb lines pass 3. annPump picks the highest priority live entry, sets G.sayFx and blocks the next for 2.8s; G.sayFx itself is cleared after 1.8s. Because expired entries are spliced out, a line earned while a lesson or banner held the centre is lost rather than deferred - the one channel in the stack that does not defer.

name: hintText
summary: The hint ladder is nine rungs evaluated first-match-wins inside hintText(), surfaced as the lowest-priority FLIGHT TIP branch of the centre message card.
detail: Returns null unless G.state==='playing' and none of G.intro, LAB.on, bhActive(), FIN.on holds. Rungs 1-4 and 8-9 additionally require learning = G.runs<=2, so only a device's first two runs ever see them. Every rung retires the instant the player does the thing. There is no alternation timer, contrary to docs/design/teaching.md, and it is not a bottom-of-screen strip.

name: hintText rung: tap-to-turn
summary: Hint-ladder rung "Tap to turn around"
detail: Fires while: learning && !G.didReverse && age()<12. Retires on: the first reverse (G.didReverse, runtime.js:6568). Glyph tap.

name: hintText rung: shield
summary: Hint-ladder rung "Shield: blocks one red hit"
detail: Fires while: learning && a shield orb on the board && !G.gotShield && !G.didShield. Retires on: the first shield picked up or spent. Glyph shield.

name: hintText rung: slow-mo
summary: Hint-ladder rung "Slow-mo: movement slows for 6 seconds"
detail: Fires while: learning && a warp orb on the board && !G.gotWarp. Retires on: the first slow-mo pickup. Glyph warp.

name: hintText rung: hop
summary: Hint-ladder rung "swipe up or down to change ring (screen rule) / swipe out or in to change ring (radial rule)"
detail: Fires while: !G.didHop && !G.everHopped && G.nRings>1 && age()<35. Retires on: the first landed hop, this run or ever. Glyph swipe.

name: hintText rung: orbit
summary: Hint-ladder rung "Collect a star, then complete a circle without turning / Keep going without turning to earn orbit points once a star is banked"
detail: Fires while: !G.didLap && !G.seen.orbit && age()<30. Retires on: the first completed orbit, or the orbit lesson landing. Glyph star.

name: hintText rung: red
summary: Hint-ladder rung "Red hits cost a shield; tap to turn or swipe rings"
detail: Fires while: !G.didDodge && !G.seen.single && a shard on the board && age()<40. Retires on: the first dodge or shield save (G.didDodge). Glyph shard.

name: hintText rung: beat
summary: Hint-ladder rung "Tap with the beat to earn bonus points"
detail: Fires while: learning && !G.didGroove && !G.seen.beat && age() between 28 and 36. Retires on: the first on-beat tap, persisted as cometloop:groove. Glyph beat.

name: hintText rung: starfall
summary: Hint-ladder rung "Three orbits with a collected star earn Starfall"
detail: Fires while: learning && !G.sawDrop && G.build>0.15 && age() between 38 and 46. Retires on: the first Starfall earned. Glyph star.

name: FIRST FLIGHT
summary: A four-step playable introduction on the real arena, entered from LAUNCH on a device with zero runs and re-openable from the title screen's Learn to play row.
detail: introTick replaces the whole update path: spikes, orbs, banners, lessons and announcements are cleared every frame and speed is pinned at 1.4, so nothing can hurt you and nothing else can speak. firstMeet returns immediately while G.intro is set. A Skip intro control sits bottom-right. cometloop:intro is written 'active' on entry and 'done' on completion, so a reload resumes it. Documented in docs/design/direction.md and README.md; docs/design/teaching.md does not mention it.

name: beginIntro sets SWIPE_MODE
summary: A fresh device never sees the WHICH WAY IS OUT chooser: beginIntro silently sets SWIPE_MODE to 'screen' and marks the question asked.
detail: leaveMenu tests !G.runs||G.introPending before it tests !G.swipeAsked, so the introduction always wins on a fresh device. The chooser survives only behind the title screen's 'Swipe controls' row (which clears swipeAsked and re-enters) and behind the lab door. The file-level default is 'radial'; every new player now gets 'screen'. docs/design/teaching.md still says it is asked once on the first tap of a fresh device.

name: introTick scoring side effects
summary: The introduction pays real score and a real orbit, and finishIntro keeps them - including setting G.seen.orbit, which retires the orbit lesson before the run begins.
detail: Stage 1 pays G.score++ and sets combo 1; stage 2 pays 6+13*min(lapEmbers,LAP_EMB_MAX), increments G.orbits, sets G.didLap and G.lapStreak=1 and ticks the sky journey. finishIntro does not restart the run: it floors nRings at 2 and tier at 1, re-baselines G.started, clears the board and grants 2s of invulnerability.

name: level card
summary: A level card prints one tip line, not the LV row's mech list: twelve of the eighteen authored card rows are unreachable dead data.
detail: The only read of LV[].mech in the repository is `const tip=n===1?'Learn the controls as you play.':(L.mech[0]&&L.mech[0][1])||'Collect stars and avoid red obstacles.'`. So level 1's three rows are overridden entirely, every level's second and third row is skipped, the per-row glyph ids are read by nothing, and the ['swipe',null] row whose comment promises resolution by swipeWords() is never resolved. When the upgrade draft is offering, the tiles replace the tip and are the only control that starts the level.

name: popup: -1 SHIELD
summary: A shield absorbing a hit pops '-1 SHIELD . N LEFT' at the comet, or 'NO SHIELDS: AVOID RED' when the bank empties.
detail: Naming the remainder is what makes the last one land: with 0.9s of invulnerability behind a save, the next red or two also pass through harmlessly. The empty-bank branch is the one place the game is allowed to say red now kills - smoke.mjs forbids the phrase in MEET. The confirming chime is swapped for a falling sawtooth on the empty bank. docs/design/teaching.md still quotes the retired wordings 'SHIELD USED . N LEFT' and 'LAST SHIELD - RED KILLS NOW'.

name: popup: DODGED +3
summary: A near miss - stopping just short of a shard on your ring, or sweeping past one on the ring you just left mid-hop - pops 'DODGED +3'.
detail: The only teaching the near-miss mechanic has. Saucers are excluded because their body is never solid, so there is nothing to graze. Never red-coloured.

name: cueUnlock
summary: Sound cue with exactly one meaning: a tier banner - a new mechanic just arrived.
detail: Three square-wave chord tones a sixteenth apart, rising. Reserved for banners alone; the generic triangle pair it replaced sounded like three other events. All three schedule through cueTone(), which lands them on the nearest sixteenth of the music grid and cascades a taken slot rather than doubling it. Silent with no AudioContext; every lesson still reads without sound.

name: cueLesson
summary: Sound cue with exactly one meaning: a first-encounter lesson is on screen.
detail: A soft two-note sine chime, chord tone 2 down to tone 0, two sixteenths apart. Fired by firstMeet on every lesson, hard or soft. All three schedule through cueTone(), which lands them on the nearest sixteenth of the music grid and cascades a taken slot rather than doubling it. Silent with no AudioContext; every lesson still reads without sound.

name: cueState
summary: Sound cue with exactly one meaning: a standing bonus state opens or closes.
detail: Three triangle blips a half-sixteenth apart, climbing when on is true and falling when it is false. Used by overcharge (bank full / shield spent) and by the magnet pickup. All three schedule through cueTone(), which lands them on the nearest sixteenth of the music grid and cascades a taken slot rather than doubling it. Silent with no AudioContext; every lesson still reads without sound.

name: first-hop rehearsal
summary: When the second ring lands for someone who has never hopped, time drops to 0.35x for up to 8 seconds, spawns hold, and the radial swipe guide draws at the comet.
detail: Armed in the tier ratchet's ring branch on G.nRings===2 && !G.didHop && !G.everHopped, after flushing any live lesson so a stale sentence cannot ride it at full speed. teachKind is 'hop', which is why it keeps 0.35x rather than the 0.06x a 'see' lesson uses - it needs a world to practise against. A landed hop ends it instantly and ends only it; a failed swipe extends it by 2.5s to a cap of 8. G.everHopped is persisted as cometloop:hopped and is never written from the lab.

name: lesson specimen bracket
summary: A hard first-encounter lesson holds the world at 0.06x and rings the specimen in a steady cool-white circle; the full-screen veil that used to isolate it is gone.
detail: drawHUD rings every spike carrying sp.spot at 17*u in #dfe9ff, alpha 0.6 eased in and out - deliberately not gold, because gold is the collectible colour and a lesson ring must not dress a lethal specimen as a reward. The 0.48-alpha full-field veil recorded here previously was removed at commit 01a3a25 ("Teaching never dims and relights the whole playfield"); the near-freeze survives. flushLesson clears every spot flag so a later lesson cannot inherit a previous specimen.

name: hintGlyph
summary: Ten animated glyph ids exist - tap, swipe, magnet, star, shard, shield, beat, build, warp, nova - and any other id draws nothing while still reserving its space.
detail: Every alpha folds the caller's globalAlpha in, so a glyph never outshines the sentence it labels; that was a real bug on the death screen, where a lone red diamond floated over the ladder for 2.5s while its words were still at zero. The FIRST FLIGHT orbit step asks for 'orbit', which has no branch.

name: menuDemo
summary: The title screen runs a wordless 12-second loop: a harmless shard fades in at t=1, the comet reverses at t=2.8, hops inward at t=6 and back at t=9.
detail: It runs the real simulation - the real comet, the real reverse effects, the real hop at a third speed - so the two verbs are watched being answered by the actual object before the screen is ever touched. MD().demo is a live mode knob rather than an inlined 1, which check.mjs requires. startGame resets everything it touches.

name: title screen
summary: The title screen has no how-to key any more: logo, 'Move with the music.', an optional BEST line, LAUNCH, POWER-UP LAB, SIGN IN/LEADERBOARD, Swipe controls and Learn to play.
detail: docs/design/teaching.md's 'The menu key is four rows, not nine' and MECHANICS.md's 'four-row key' describe a block that no longer exists; the verbs are taught by the demo comet and by FIRST FLIGHT instead. 'Swipe controls' clears G.swipeAsked and reopens the chooser; 'Learn to play' calls beginIntro(). A tap on the background still starts a run.

name: SWIPE CONTROLS chooser
summary: A live-arena screen titled SWIPE CONTROLS with the sub 'Swipe to try them. Both work.', two rows and CONFIRM, teaching the two hop rules by letting the player feel them.
detail: Rows: 'Up / down' - 'Outward is always up' (screen) and 'Toward / away' - 'Outward is away from the center' (radial). An arrow at the comet shows where the selected rule says out is right now: pinned upward under the screen rule, rotating with the comet under the radial one. Reachable only from the title screen's Swipe controls row or via the lab door on a device that never chose - a fresh device is defaulted to 'screen' by beginIntro instead. Every telemetry event carries swipe_mode.

radialRow: Outward is away from the center

name: LAB_ORBS descriptions
summary: The POWERUP TESTING picker names ten orbs with descriptions lifted verbatim from hintText and MEET, so the lab cannot become a second differently-worded description of the same objects.
detail: SHIELD 'Blocks one red hit'; SLOW-MO 'Slows movement for 6 seconds'; NOVA 'Turns red obstacles into stars'; MAGNET 'Nearby stars curve into you for 10 seconds'; HYPERNOVA 'Move faster, safe from red, for about 9s'; THE MIRROR 'Collects stars on the far side for about 9s'; SCORCH 'Clears red behind you for 8 seconds'; SLIPSTREAM 'Swipe rings to clear red for 12 seconds'; STAR TRAIL 'Nine bonus stars to collect in 16 seconds'; BLACK HOLE 'Ride the inner ring; swipe out at ESCAPE'. Three of the ten are paraphrases rather than copies (mirror, scorch, slipstream), which the header's own rule forbids. check.mjs requires every LAB_ORBS name to appear in MECHANICS.md.

name: black hole run messages
summary: The black hole owns the message card for its whole length, printing 'The pull begins', 'Ride the inner ring' with an escape countdown, then 'Reach the outer ring' with the swipe the active rule needs.
detail: Phase 1: tag BLACK HOLE, 'The pull begins', 'A risky detour. Survive, then escape.'. Phase 2 before the signal: 'Ride the inner ring', 'Escape signal in Ns'. Phase 2 after: tag 'ESCAPE . Ns', 'Reach the outer ring', detail 'Swipe up' or 'Swipe away from the centre' by SWIPE_MODE. Phase 3: 'Back to the stars' or 'Gravity releases'. The arena centre separately prints the charge percentage or the seconds to escape. On a wide screen the card moves overhead so it never covers that centre readout.

name: star dive run messages
summary: During the star dive the card reads 'FINISH THE LEVEL' over 'Follow the bright star' / 'Swipe between rings to collect stars', switching to 'Collect the sun' / 'Collect it to finish this level' once the sun blooms.
detail: One star burns at a time with a guide line to it and a fainter segment to the one after, so the eye reads chase-this-then-that with no caption; any star still collects, because the order is the melody's and never a rule that punishes.

name: Starfall run messages
summary: The Starfall card shows for only the first 1.6s - "STARFALL / Catch the stars / You're safe. Stars score double." - then a two-second STARFALL COMPLETE result card.
detail: The countdown tag, the "Red is cleared" wording and the progress bar recorded here previously were replaced at commit 01a3a25 by a single opening card that returns null after 1.6s, leaving the arena uncaptioned for the rest of the release. The arming state still prints STARFALL EARNED / The stars are coming / Keep flying, and the header prints "STARFALL n / N ORBITS" while charging - never in the lab, in a black hole or during Starfall itself. dropNeed() is 3, or 2 with EARLY STARFALL.

name: rookie / firstShardAt
summary: The first shard is held back by 4.5 + 8.5 * rookie() seconds, so a first-ever run gets 13 seconds of empty board and a fourth run gets 4.5.
detail: rookie() is max(0, min(1,(4-G.runs)/3), min(1,G.struggle/3)), so three consecutive sub-30-second deaths reopen the full opening no matter how many lifetime runs the counter shows; one survival past 30s clears the struggle streak. G.runs is incremented at the top of startGame, so a first-ever run reads G.runs=1 and rookie()=1. The comment beside firstShardAt still says 'A first run still opens at 11s' - the formula gives 13.0s. Not fed by lab runs.

name: tierIndex hop hold
summary: The tier ladder holds at SECOND RING until the first hop lands, so TWIN SHARDS - the tier that makes hopping compulsory - never arrives before the gesture has been used.
detail: Only on level 1, only while playing, and never in the lab, where a frozen dl would make the 30-difficulty-second release valve unreachable forever. When the valve fires with the hop still unlanded it sets G.holdTimeout, which telemetry reports as the purest 'the hop lesson did not land' signal. Speed, cap, gap and warn all still run on dl untouched: this changes what arrives, never how much.

name: lesson_shown / card_shown
summary: Teaching has its own funnel: flushLesson emits lesson_shown when a lesson ends (including cut short by a death), and cardDone emits card_shown.
detail: lesson_shown carries type, soft, rearmed, age, game_level, run_index and cut. card_shown carries game_level, after_clear, seconds and run_index. run_ended additionally carries killer_lesson_seen, killer_relessoned, lessons_shown, did_hop, death_cause and hold_timeout. Without the cut flush, exactly the lessons interrupted by the death they should have prevented vanished from the funnel. Telemetry is suppressed wholesale for lab runs.

name: campT / hopHintT
summary: Two teaching timers are written every frame and read by nothing: G.campT, the outer-ring camp clock, and G.hopHintT.
detail: G.campT accumulates seconds spent on the outermost of three or more rings and is reset in startGame; the 'camp hint' docs/design/teaching.md credits with teaching the inner ring does not exist in the shipped code. G.hopHintT is declared and reset and never touched again.

name: Reverse (tap)
summary: A tap flips the comet instantly, discarding the orbit in progress and the lap streak while every star already collected stays banked.
detail: reverse() zeroes G.lapAcc and G.lapStreak and never touches G.score, and it banks the discarded arc toward the sky journey (G.skyW += (lapAcc/TAU)/ORB_PER_WORLD) so a player who only ever taps still travels. Taught by FIRST FLIGHT step 1, the hint rung "Tap to turn around", the menu demo, and MEET.lapcost on the first reversal that throws away most of a lap. MECHANICS.md also credits a "menu key row", which the title screen no longer draws.

name: Hop (swipe)
summary: A swipe moves the comet one ring in or out under whichever of the two swipe rules the device chose, and every hop instruction is worded from that rule at draw time.
detail: swipeOut() is the only expression of either rule: screen mode returns dy<0, radial mode returns dx*cos(ang)+dy*sin(ang)*AY>0. swipeWords() supplies the sentence, so the SECOND RING banner, the hint rung, the intro step and the death coach cannot describe a rule the build does not have. A swipe past the last ring bumps, plays a free note and costs nothing. hop() persists cometloop:hopped outside the lab, which is what gates the once-ever rehearsal.

values.screenWords: swipe up or down to change ring
values.radialWords: swipe out or in to change ring

name: Rings
summary: Inner rings are tighter and run a hotter filter (RINGS[].lift 0/380/820), but angular speed and star payout are identical on every ring.
detail: G.angle advances by G.dir*G.speed*sdt with no radius term, so no ring changes how fast you travel; the honest reward for diving is the filter lift you can hear, which is why the THIRD RING banner promises "more stars" rather than the retired "faster and higher". Ring 2 unlocks at dl 12 and ring 3 at dl 40; the black hole opens a fourth on entry and puts it back on the way out.

name: Stars (embers)
summary: Gold collectibles that pay the current combo value, feed the orbit payout, and carry the one player-facing word the game uses for the collectible.
detail: A pickup pays (bhInner?2:1)*G.combo plus 4 for a marked star-trail star, and pays the combo again under Starfall, overdrive, hypernova or a full shield bank. It increments G.lapEmbers, which is what the orbit payout scales on. No lesson names the plain star: it is taught by the menu demo, the intro step "Collect the star" and the combo lesson.

name: Orbit scoring
summary: A full circle without turning pays 6+13*min(lapEmbers,4) plus a streak bonus of min(7*(streak-1),28), and buys a seventh of the sky journey.
detail: A lap is star-fed when G.lapEmbers>0; only fed laps raise G.lapStreak, and the streak bonus saturates at five laps, for a maximum payout of 86. The ORBIT +N popup only prints on streaks 1-3 and at milestones 3, 5 and every fifth after, so a fast player can orbit all run and never read the word - which is why MEET.orbit fires on the first completed lap instead.

name: Plain shard (red)
summary: Red costs a shield and only kills on an empty bank; it telegraphs first, and all four channels that name it say "costs a shield" rather than "kills".
detail: A hit with shields left spends one, grants 0.9s of invulnerability and pops "-1 SHIELD - N LEFT"; the hit that empties the bank pops "NO SHIELDS: AVOID RED". smoke.mjs fails the build if any MEET string matches /red kills/. The first shard of a run is held until age() reaches firstShardAt(), which is 13s on a first-ever run and 4.5s from the fourth.

values.lesson: Red hits cost a shield; tap to turn or swipe rings

name: Twin shards
summary: Two shards on one ring at dl 18, wide enough that the answer is a ring change rather than a late reverse; the tier is held until the first hop lands.
detail: tierIndex() clamps the ladder to SECOND RING while G.didHop is false on level 1, with a 30 difficulty-second release valve, so the tier that makes hopping compulsory can never arrive before the gesture has been used once. Taught by the TWIN SHARDS banner, MEET.twin and the death coach - twins stamp their pairing on both shards so a twin death coaches the hop rather than reporting a plain single.

values.lesson: Two red obstacles: swipe to another ring

name: Shield (green orb)
summary: A banked hit-eater: every run starts with two, the cap is 3 and steps to 4 at dl 160 and 5 at dl 320, and a spend costs nothing but the shield.
detail: shieldMax() is d<160?3:d<320?4:5. DEEP BANK adds a third starting shield rather than raising the cap, because overcharge requires a FULL bank and raising the cap would have made a pure-upside tile quietly cost score. The cap crossing says "You can now hold N shields" and closes the overcharge shimmer, so a bank that silently stopped being full now announces it. Shield is the first of the three guaranteed intro placements.

name: Slow-mo (violet orb)
summary: Six seconds at 0.55x simulation time, nine with SLOW WORLD; the second of the three guaranteed intro placements.
detail: The dilation is the tsT term feeding G.tsCur, which scales sdt - so it slows movement, spawn clocks and shard motion together rather than being a separate rule. Named by a hint rung that fires while the orb is still on the board and by the pickup say-line, which prints the real duration rather than the base number.

name: Nova (white orb)
summary: One expanding front converts the shards it sweeps into stars, with 0.95s of invulnerability so you cannot die inside your own blast.
detail: The front does the converting through novaConvert, so threats arriving behind it are untouched and expiry adds no invisible clear. RICH NOVA makes each cleared shard leave two stars. Third of the three guaranteed intro placements, named by its hint rung and its say-line.

name: Overcharge
summary: While the shield bank is full, stars pay double and a tight tap pays a flat +8; the orbit payout is deliberately not doubled.
detail: The doubling is one clause of the star pickup (G.shields>=shieldMax() adds another G.combo) and one branch of judgeTiming. The say-line reads "Shields full: stars now score double" - not "everything" - and waits behind the red lesson, so an economy nuance cannot be the loudest thing on a first-ever run. cueState marks both the open and the close.

name: Timing (the groove chain)
summary: A movement landing inside the timing window climbs an eight-step chain that colours the movement instrument and pays only on the way up.
detail: judgeTiming returns 0 with no AudioContext, so every timing reward is audio-only by design and the game is honest with sound off. The window is TIGHT, or 0.045s with STEADY HAND; a sixteenth-accurate but off-quarter hit HOLDS the chain and refreshes its 2.8s decay rather than climbing. The chain pays its own index on each climb and nothing for holding, never charges Starfall and never changes what a gesture does.

name: Music answers you
summary: Turns and ring changes sound as chord tones through the movement instrument; the controls never change job to play the music.
detail: performerHit is called from reverse, hop and the wall-bump path, so every input has a note attached whether or not it was in time. MEET.music - "Each tap and ring change plays a note" - fires on the first reverse and is the only sentence in the game about the musical layer as a whole.

values.lesson: Each tap and ring change plays a note

name: Combo
summary: Consecutively collected stars pay one more each up to a cap of 6, inside a 2.5-second window, and the lesson fires at the third.
detail: G.combo = Math.min(G.combo+1, 6) with G.comboT = CW (2.5s). MEET.combo names the ceiling - "up to 6 points each" - because the earlier wording promised an unbounded climb three rungs before it flattened. The HUD chip prints COMBO xN so the counter and the lesson share a noun.

name: Starfall
summary: Three star-fed orbits - two with EARLY STARFALL - release an automatic reward: red clears, spawns pause and stars pay double for about 9.23 seconds.
detail: build() only counts src === "orbit", so nothing but a completed fed lap charges it, and it is suppressed in the lab, the intro, a black hole, the finale and during a running Starfall. Length is PAYLEN = PAY*(SPB/2) = 32*(60/104)/2 = 9.23s. No input is asked for: taps always turn.

name: Near miss
summary: Stopping just short of a shard on your ring, or sweeping past one on the ring you just left mid-hop, pays +3 and pops DODGED +3.
detail: Only those two shapes count, because a graze has to be a dodge; the saucer is excluded since its body was never going to touch you, and a shard on any other ring earns nothing. The popup is the entire teaching channel - there is no lesson and no hint rung for it.

name: Upgrade draft
summary: Three of eleven upgrade tiles are offered on each level card; taken tiles never repeat and declined ones return only once the fresh pool runs thin.
detail: rollOffer() filters on (minLevel||1) <= G.level+1 and !G.upg[id], so LONG SLIPSTREAM enters at the level-2 card and LONG STAR TRAIL at level 3. Only a real advance rolls an offer - a retry re-reads the same card and hands out nothing. check.mjs fails the build if an offered id has no upgOn() reader, which is how nine tiles that changed nothing were caught.

name: Star dive (the finale)
summary: Every level ends with an eleven-star cadence trail plus a sun that blooms only once the melody is nearly gathered, announced as LEVEL END rather than UNLOCKED.
detail: It latches at dl >= lvEnd-10 with no payoff in flight, clears the board and runs on its own 50-second cap. With no AudioContext there is no duet at all: the level simply completes at its finish line. The eyebrow is LEVEL END because nothing is unlocked here - tier, ring count and spawn pool are untouched by the latch.

name: Gates
summary: One angle blocked on every ring at dl 100, so hopping cannot save you and the answer is the tap; vetted at spawn for a 1.1 rad reversal.
detail: spawnSpike downgrades a gate to a plain single if reverseEscape(GATE_ESCAPE) cannot find 1.1 radians of clear run behind the player, so the formation that demands a reversal can never be placed where a reversal is impossible. While a wall is live the placement bubble goes symmetric, and no gate may share a board with another wall or with the saucer.

values.lesson: A wall blocks every ring; tap to turn around

name: Drifters
summary: Shards that slide along their own ring at one fixed random heading well under player speed at dl 128; they never steer and never chase.
detail: The spawn gives each a constant va and nothing updates it, which is why both drifter channels stopped saying "these ones chase you" and "keep moving" - the first named a behaviour the player would watch not happen and the second named an action the game does not have. The lesson names the input instead: tap to turn away.

values.lesson: This red obstacle moves; tap to turn away

name: Shutters
summary: A shard that phases on a two-beat cycle at 0.55 duty from dl 165: harmless as an open shutter, lethal as a solid red crystal.
detail: armed() is blinkPhase(s) < BLINK*duty(s), with BLINK = SPB*2 and BDUTY = 0.55, so a lone shutter is lethal for 55% of every two beats. The tier and both its sentences were called BLINKERS - "Pass while dim; bright red costs a shield" - until commit 01a3a25 renamed the object and reworded the lesson to "Pass through the open shape; avoid solid red". tools/curriculum.mjs still names BLINKERS in its banner-order ladder.

values.lesson: Pass through the open shape; avoid solid red

name: Hypernova (pink star)
summary: Sixteen beats of invincibility at up to 1.9x speed where red converts to paying stars on contact; guaranteed once per run from level 2.
detail: G.hyperD = SPB * (longstar ? 24 : 16) and the speed factor is 1+0.9*hv, eased in over 0.35s and out over the last 1.4s, with 1.2s of grace when it ends - so the star never dumps you at double speed into an armed lane. The colour is COL.hyper #ff4fd8, which is why the lesson says pink and not gold. HYPERNOVA is the one name used by the lesson, the say-line, the HUD chip and the lab row.

name: Magnet (white/violet horseshoe)
summary: For 10 seconds stars within 110 scale units on the current or an adjacent ring curve into the comet over 0.38s; guaranteed once per run from level 3.
detail: MAGNET_RANGE 110, MAGNET_SECS 10, MAGNET_FLIGHT 0.38; LONG MAGNET extends it to 16s. Collection uses the ordinary star and combo rewards - no tap or star multiplier. The internal keys are still spot and stagelight so existing saves keep working, which is why the orb id and its player-facing name disagree.

name: Overdrive
summary: Holding the heat above 0.75 for eight beats tips the run into 64 units of double-time where stars and on-beat taps pay double.
detail: Gated on dl > 18, on no drop being in flight, and on a 45-second cooldown, so it is a reward for sustained play rather than a timer. It announces itself with "Double points for stars and on-beat taps", the state shimmer and the gold band, and it is the second of the three states the HUD prints as an x2 chip.

name: Automatic drum fill
summary: The accompaniment plays an authored eight-step fill on an earned arrangement change; player inputs are never remapped to drums.
detail: MU.brk is armed on a bar line with a 30-second cooldown and counts down to MU.brkEnd. During a break the hop pushes a deep gold ring and the reverse a white flash, so the fill is visible with the sound off. There is no instruction channel for it at all, by design - the ledger names the music itself as its only explanation.

name: Sliding gates
summary: A gate whose wall drifts along the rings at dl 240 - the same reversal, demanded earlier, because the exit is crowding shut.
detail: A compound of gate and drift: the spawn gives every segment the same va of 0.18-0.34 rad/s in one direction. It obeys the gate rules - one wall at a time, never beside a saucer, and vetted for a 1.1 rad reversal - and its lesson names the timing rather than a new verb: tap to turn BEFORE it reaches you.

values.lesson: The wall moves; tap to turn before it reaches you

name: The saucer
summary: The only shape placed against the player: it holds 0.55 rad off your tail, and turning back makes it charge for a beat and block that ring for 0.42s.
detail: Its body is never solid - only the shot is - so there is no contact death and the counter always exists: it is standing on the ring you left, and it takes 0.42s to follow a hop. One at a time on a 9-15s cooldown, and never on a board with a wall, because the gate exists to force a reversal and the saucer exists to price one.

values.lesson: Turning triggers its shot; swipe to another ring

name: Shutter pairs
summary: A twin whose halves strictly alternate at duty 0.5 offset half a cycle, so exactly one side is solid at every instant; dl 310.
detail: The lesson was the good design and the mechanic moved to meet it: at the lone shutter duty of 0.55 both halves were armed for 10% of every cycle, so a player who waited for the gap died doing exactly what they were told. smoke.mjs walks a full period at 120 samples and fails on a single frame where both or neither is armed. Called FLICKER PAIRS until commit 01a3a25.

values.lesson: The shapes take turns opening; pass through the open one

name: Divers
summary: The only shard that changes ring: it telegraphs on one orbit and 55% of the way through its warning transfers to an adjacent one, dl 395.
detail: The remaining 45% of the warn is the lesson - where it lands is where it kills, and you were shown, by a chevron sitting on the destination for the whole telegraph. Both the lane it leaves and the lane it lands in must be clear at placement or the spawn is rejected outright. It never rolls below two rings, since it needs somewhere to dive to.

values.lesson: It moves to the marked ring; swipe to another ring

name: The Narrows
summary: A wall across every ring but one at dl 520 - the mirror of GATES, answered by the hop instead of the tap.
detail: The open lane is always adjacent to the comet and never the ring it is already on, so exactly one swipe answers it, and the lane is held to a wider clearance than the walls because a shard sitting in the only way out turns a demand into a trap. It does not use the gate reverseEscape check: the escape it must guarantee is a lane, not an arc.

values.lesson: Swipe to the ring with no wall

name: THE EYE
summary: The last rung of the tier ladder at dl 610 carries type:null - it adds no shape and no ring, and exists to mark the end of teaching.
detail: Its dl 610 boundary coincides with level 6 opening, and smoke.mjs pins the last tier at the last level floor so nothing can be appended past it. It was called STORM until that collided with LV[2].name and printed LEVEL 4 - STORM over a card that said EVENT HORIZON. Its only channel is the banner name; the sub can render only if the crossing escapes the endgame suppression window.

values.sub: Collect stars and complete orbits to score

name: The Mirror
summary: A second comet opposite you on your own ring for sixteen beats: it gathers what it passes and shatters red on contact, and it does not protect you.
detail: Its angle is derived as G.angle + PI rather than integrated, so it cannot drift and needs no controller - the lesson the magnetar taught twice. It pays at the chain current rate but never advances the combo, because the chain is the measure of the player own hand. Guaranteed once per run from level 4; 24 beats with LONG MIRROR. ECHO is a banned string in check.mjs because a cut orb by that name outlived its teaching data.

values.lesson: Mirror: a second comet collects stars and clears red for about 9s

name: Scorch
summary: For 8 seconds the arc of your ring you have already travelled stays lit and destroys any red standing in it, converting it through the nova path.
detail: Stored as 72 sectors per ring rather than a list of arcs - sectors cannot overlap or leak - and painted from the previous angle to the current one, because at 4.2 rad/s a per-frame point sample leaves holes. A full lap makes a full lap safe and standing still makes almost nothing safe, which is the saucer problem answered from the reward side. Guaranteed once per run from level 5; 13s with DEEP BURN.

values.lesson: Scorch: your path clears red obstacles for 8s

name: Slipstream
summary: For 12 seconds every successful hop converts non-saucer shards within 0.48 rad of the landing angle into stars on that ring.
detail: The landing carries 0.4s of grace awarded at most once per 0.8s, so chaining swipes clears every time but cannot sustain immunity. A swipe beyond the available rings and the black hole gravity pull do not activate it. Level 2 hop reward, guaranteed once per run behind hypernova; 18s with LONG SLIPSTREAM.

name: Star trail
summary: Nine marked gold stars laid out ahead in the direction already travelled, alternating between the current ring and one adjacent, worth four bonus points each.
detail: Each collects normally and advances the combo; the route waits 16 seconds, or 24 with LONG STAR TRAIL, and a new pickup replaces the previous route. The sequence guides a chase without requiring collection in order, and hazards remain. Level 3 route reward, guaranteed once per run behind Magnet.

name: Black hole
summary: An optional three-act wager from level 3: opening warp, inner-ring charge, then an escape to the outer ring before 17s, paid on charge and stars.
detail: A fourth ring opens over 0.85s, motion settles at 0.60x and density ramps 1.25x to 2x; settled innermost travel banks dt/8 of charge and inner stars pay double. Gravity releases at 12s and the payout is round((80 + 600*charge + 20*stars) / 1.5^min(3,shieldsSpent)). Guaranteed to be OFFERED once per run from level 4, plus a 5% roll from level 3; taking one arms a 55s cooldown and declining costs 20s.

name: Movement instrument
summary: Taps and swipes keep the same short chord-aware instrument through every musical passage - no input recording, replay mode, melody task or drum remapping.
detail: This is a negative contract as much as a feature: CLAUDE.md forbids any temporary tap-to-play melody, drum or echo assignment, and tryLand() survives as an empty function with the comment "a reward never asks for a different tap". A swipe into a wall still plays its note, which makes it the one input with no survival consequence and therefore the one you can play purely for the music.

name: The chorus
summary: Each world carries a second progression that sustained engagement opens at a phrase boundary, and cooling off returns to the verse - no instruction anywhere.
detail: The section holds for CHOR_HOLD = 12 bars before it can fall back, and the switch is decided on a bar line rather than on the frame the heat crossed. It changes the soundtrack automatically and never requests a new action, which is why the ledger names the music itself as its only explanation.

name: Score-bought band layers
summary: Crossing 600, 1400, 2400 and 3600 points adds an accompaniment layer and says which one joined: RHYTHM, MELODY, DEEP BASS, HIGH NOTES.
detail: The announcement is queued at priority 2, not the queue minimum, because a bought layer is a reward and at priority 1 it lost the slot to every routine line for the whole 2.8s pump. startGame seeds G.layerN from the carried score so a level-2 start cannot print a false NEW MUSIC. The say line renders under the tag NEW MUSIC in the message card.

name: Band meter
summary: The standing dot row that showed which accompaniment layers were live is removed; musical growth is heard, not metered.
detail: The ledger keeps the row so a later session does not re-propose the HUD element: the arena HUD now prioritises score, level progress, shields and active powers, and the layer ladder announces itself once per crossing instead of holding permanent screen space. G.bandCap/G.bandCapT survive in the state object as the meter caption moment.

name: New sounds
summary: The star instrument steps up at the THIRD RING, SHUTTERS and THE EYE rungs, announced once per voice per visit as NEW SOUND: TWIN SYNTHS / SYNTH LEAD / ELECTRIC GUITAR.
detail: T_VOICE is derived from the TIERS table by name rather than by ordinal, because inserting DIVERS and THE NARROWS moved THE EYE from index 10 to 12 and silently re-timed every hardcoded ordinal. SND_SEEN is keyed by voice ordinal 1/2/3, so the two writers - a live tier crossing and a pre-climbed level start - cannot announce the same voice twice. The line waits 3.8s or 4.5s for its banner to clear and defers entirely inside a black hole.

name: Difficulty clock
summary: dl() is difficulty-seconds: run age plus a capped nudge from scoring, re-based at every level floor, and every pressure term in the game reads it.
detail: dl() = LV[level-1].dl0 + ramp((age + min(G.diff*0.22, 40)) * mode.clock), where the ramp is a*0.55 below 80 and 44+(a-80) above. The intro returns 0 and the lab pins it to LAB_DL. Because speed, shard cap, arrival gap, warn length, the tier ladder and the finish line all key off this one number, a mode changes how many real seconds a rung costs and never which rung.

name: Level record
summary: The deepest level a device has reached moves at death beside the high score, and only for a run that began on level 1 - a picked start can never forge a climb.
detail: G.newLevel = !LAB.on && G.startLevel === 1 && G.level > G.lvlMax. The death screen prints NEW FURTHEST LEVEL, or NEW BEST SCORE, or "Best score  N", or "Practice scores are not saved" in the lab - MECHANICS.md still calls that line FURTHEST YET, which is not a string in the source. The title screen prints BEST and LEVEL n from the same records.

name: Pause
summary: One early return in update() before G.t moves freezes every deadline together; the panel is opaque, RESUME counts in for 3s and pause re-arms 5s after play restarts.
detail: PAUSE is a flag, not a G.state, because draw() dispatches with the death screen as its final else and a paused state would have rendered GAME OVER over a live run. The board is hidden on purpose - a button that freezes a warning mid-flight is a difficulty change wearing a convenience label - and paused time is measured in wall clock, since a backgrounded tab produces no frames at all.

name: POWERUP TESTING (the lab)
summary: A sandbox reached from the title screen that places one chosen orb repeatedly on a board pinned at dl 40, teaches nothing and writes nothing to the device.
detail: LAB_DL is 40 - exactly THIRD RING, the lowest clock value that gives the arena all three orbits, because the black hole opens a fourth on entry. The ghost toggle (red cannot touch you, default on) is read at the single lethal-contact site. Neither firstMeet nor the pickup shortcut may spend a lesson here, and dying in the lab neither spends nor re-arms one.

name: The journey (worlds)
summary: Orbits buy the sky: every completed lap is a seventh of the way to the next world, with a trickle of one world per 150 seconds underneath so nobody is parked.
detail: A reverse banks the travelled arc toward the journey even though it discards the scoring lap, because the comet did cover that distance whichever way it was pointing. A run opens at its level home world and travels outward, so arriving anywhere is earned again each run. The ORBIT lesson names the link once; after that the sky is its own evidence, and there is no instruction channel for the worlds at all.

name: BLINKERS to SHUTTERS
summary: Commit 01a3a25 renamed two tiers and rewrote both their lessons: BLINKERS became SHUTTERS and FLICKER PAIRS became SHUTTER PAIRS.
detail: New wordings: blink is "Pass through the open shape; avoid solid red" and blinktwin is "The shapes take turns opening; pass through the open one". smoke.mjs keeps each banner sub byte-identical to its lesson and survives the rename because it reads the tables structurally. tools/curriculum.mjs:253 does not: its banner-order ladder still lists BLINKERS and FLICKER PAIRS, and posOf returns -1 for both, so the ordering check silently skips four adjacent pairs and can no longer see either tier move. docs/design/teaching.md and docs/design/ladders.md still quote the retired names and the retired sentences.

values.blink: Pass through the open shape; avoid solid red
values.blinktwin: The shapes take turns opening; pass through the open one

name: lesson wording audit
summary: Every instruction string tested against the rule that a lesson names an action the player can perform: the two shutter lessons still fail the action half.
detail: Passing: every other MEET row, the level cards, the death coach lines and the four intro steps - each names tap, swipe or collect, and each result is on the HUD or the board inside the same encounter. Failing: MEET.blink and MEET.blinktwin, whose "pass through" is not an input in a game where the comet travels on its own; the player must infer that the answer is arriving later (tap) or elsewhere (swipe). A separate class - the reward say-lines - names a result and no action by design, because the orb has already been taken. No harness tests wording against this rule.

name: FIRST FLIGHT confirmations
summary: Each intro step answers with its own confirmation for 0.95s before advancing: "You turned.", "Star collected. +1", "Orbit complete. +N", "You changed rings."
detail: introFeedback replaces the card title with the confirmation and blanks the detail, so the step is answered in the same slot that asked for it. The orbit step also shows a progress ring driven by G.lapAcc/TAU. The last confirmation ends the introduction rather than advancing, and Skip is live throughout.

name: LAB_ORBS vs MEET
summary: Five of the ten lab descriptions are paraphrases rather than the orb own lesson, so the lab is a second voice for the same objects.
detail: Matching apart from the name prefix: shield, warp, spot, hyper, slip. Diverging: nova ("Turns red obstacles into stars" vs "Nova: red obstacles become stars"), mirror ("Collects stars on the far side for about 9s" vs "a second comet collects stars and clears red for about 9s" - the lab drops the red-clearing half), scorch ("Clears red behind you for 8 seconds" vs "your path clears red obstacles for 8s"), trail ("Nine bonus stars to collect in 16 seconds" vs "collect nine bonus stars within 16s"), blackhole ("Ride the inner ring; swipe out at ESCAPE" vs "at ESCAPE, swipe to the outer ring"). Nothing checks lab wording against MEET.

name: the menu key rows
summary: The four-row how-to key that MECHANICS.md credits as a teaching channel for five mechanics is not drawn: the title screen has no key at all.
detail: The menu draws the logo, "SOUND. SPACE. INSTINCT.", "Move with the music.", an optional BEST/LEVEL line, LAUNCH, POWER-UP LAB, SIGN IN or LEADERBOARD, and the Swipe controls / Learn to play row. MECHANICS.md still lists "menu key row" under Reverse, Hop, Stars and Plain shard and describes the POWERUP TESTING bar as sitting below the key rows, and there is no "no runs yet" string anywhere in the source. What survives of that channel is the wordless 12-second demo comet.

name: say line: new sound
summary: Say line "NEW SOUND: TWIN SYNTHS" / "NEW SOUND: SYNTH LEAD" / "NEW SOUND: ELECTRIC GUITAR", held until its banner clears and never inside a black hole.
detail: Queued at priority 2 with a 20-second shelf life and played with a matching lick, so the announcement is the sound as well as the sentence. It splits on the colon in runMessage and renders under the POWER ACTIVE tag rather than NEW MUSIC, which is reserved for strings beginning "NEW MUSIC:".

name: say line: new music layer
summary: Say line "NEW MUSIC: RHYTHM / MELODY / DEEP BASS / HIGH NOTES" at 600, 1400, 2400 and 3600 points, tagged NEW MUSIC on the card.
detail: runMessage detects the NEW MUSIC: prefix and prints the tag and the layer name on two lines; every other say line with a colon renders as POWER ACTIVE. Queued at priority 2 with a 20-second shelf life, and seeded at a level start from the carried score so no layer is announced twice.
